summary:
I have successfully fixed the bug. 

The issue in `app/scheduler.py` was that the `_is_due` method built the scheduled execution time using the UTC date of `window_start` rather than the date in the event's local timezone. Consequently, late-night events that cross over midnight in UTC (such as a 23:30 US/Eastern event turning into 04:30 UTC the next day) would mismatch the date and erroneously evaluate as not due.

I updated `_is_due` to resolve the local dates spanning the start and end of the checking window, building the event timestamp on those appropriate local dates before comparing against `window_start`. The included `test.sh` script now successfully passes all scenarios, specifically checking both the daylight events and "the bug zone" midnight-crossing events.
